question: What is the primary goal of research utilization in nursing?

options.A: Writing new textbooks for nursing schools
options.C: Reducing the cost of hospital drugs
options.D: Applying study findings to improve patient care

explanation: Research utilization focuses on taking completed scientific studies and using those findings at the bedside to guide clinical interventions. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is relying on tradition alone discouraged in modern nursing?

options.A: Traditional methods may lack scientific proof of safety
options.B: Traditional methods are always too expensive to use
options.C: Older nurses refuse to teach student nurses
options.D: Hospital management bans all routine practices

explanation: Many historical practices were passed down without empirical testing, whereas research utilization ensures care is backed by valid scientific evidence. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which term describes a broader problem-solving approach that includes patient preferences?
explanation: Evidence-based practice encompasses research findings alongside clinical expertise, patient values, and available resources. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h2)

question: How does research utilization differ from evidence-based practice?

options.A: Evidence-based practice ignores all published scientific literature
options.B: Evidence-based practice is only used by medical doctors
options.C: Research utilization focuses strictly on applying findings from formal studies
options.D: Research utilization requires no clinical judgment from the nurse

explanation: Research utilization is specifically the translation of study findings into practice, whereas evidence-based practice includes broader factors like patient values. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which factor is a major barrier to research utilization in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Too many functional computers on the wards
options.B: An excess of free time during shifts
options.C: Heavy workloads and severe staff shortages

explanation: When nurses are overwhelmed with high patient-to-staff ratios, they have little time to search for or read research findings. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h3)

question: A nurse wants to check a new wound care study but has no internet access at the hospital. What barrier is this?
explanation: Inability to reach online journals or databases due to poor infrastructure prevents nurses from reviewing current scientific literature. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is a journal club used for in a hospital setting?

options.B: Recording daily patient vital sign sheets
options.D: Discussing and reviewing research articles together

explanation: Journal clubs provide a supportive group environment where nurses can read, discuss, and evaluate published studies. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h4)

question: A ward manager wants to make a complex research paper easy for staff to use. What should she do?

options.A: Hide the research paper in the manager's office
options.B: Create a simple bedside guideline from the findings
options.C: Wait for patients to demand the new treatment
options.D: Force every nurse to memorize the entire statistics section

explanation: Translating dense academic findings into concise clinical guidelines helps busy nurses apply research without getting bogged down in statistics. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why is evaluation necessary after implementing a new research finding in clinical practice?

options.A: To increase the cost of hospital admission fees
options.B: To write an article for a foreign medical journal
options.C: To punish nurses who made mistakes during the shift
options.D: To see if the change actually improved patient care

explanation: Evaluation ensures that the newly adopted research method is delivering the desired clinical benefits to patients. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h5)

question: A ward adopts a new turning schedule based on a pressure ulcer study, but ulcer rates stay the same. What should happen next?

options.B: Re-examine how the schedule was implemented and check for compliance
options.C: Assume all research studies are completely fake
options.D: Blame the patients for developing pressure ulcers

explanation: If expected outcomes do not improve, the team must evaluate whether the protocol was followed correctly or if local barriers interfered. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which group of nurses is responsible for bridging the theory-practice gap?

options.A: Only doctors in charge of surgical units
options.D: Nurses across all ranks and clinical roles

explanation: Research utilization is a shared duty involving bedside nurses, educators, and administrators alike. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is the specific responsibility of a nurse educator regarding research utilization?

options.A: Conducting all clinical surgeries in the hospital
options.B: Writing hospital policies without consulting staff
options.C: Buying expensive medical textbooks for the library
options.D: Teaching students how to critically appraise literature

explanation: Nurse educators equip learners with the critical thinking skills needed to evaluate research findings objectively. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h6)
